declarations.standing: The witness (deliverable 2). It is a closed statement on ℝ with no instance argument. Conjunct 1 is the entry's `from` (inextensible_nested) at every open W, which is stronger than the ladder's reading at W = M. Conjunct 2 is the negation of the `to` (le_nested). Conjuncts 3–5 say the narrower rational line is causal and glues in both Lean forms of DEC-167. Conjuncts 6–9 say the same of the wider spacelike line, and add that it is causally arc-connected. The evidence lists conjuncts 1–5, 7 and 9; conjuncts 6 (spacelikeLine.IsCausal) and 8 (spacelikeLine.AbsolutelyMinimal) come from the title's 'both causal and absolutely minimal' and from the template, cutLine_separates_inextensibleNested, which carries both gluing forms for the wider causality. Proof: three conjuncts are given by causal_ladder through the ladder's edges. time_function ⇒ is_causal gives both IsCausal conjuncts, from rationalLine_hasTimeFunction and spacelikeLine_hasTimeFunction. causally_arc_connected ⇒ absolutely_minimal gives spacelikeLine.AbsolutelyMinimal. The rest are library lemmas plus rationalLine_inextensibleNestedOn_spacelikeLine.

declarations.name: Causal.Causality.inextensible_iff_of_causalCurveOn_eq
declarations.statement: (∀ ⦃d : ℝ → M⦄ ⦃a b : ℝ⦄, C.CausalCurveOn W d a b → ∀ s ∈ Icc a b, ∀ t ∈ Icc a b, d s = d t) → (C.Inextensible W I c ↔ C.CausalCurveIn W I c)   (any causality C on any topological space M, any open W, interval I, curve c; no instance)
declarations.standing: Deliverable 1, the model-free lemma, as the evidence words it.

declarations.name: Causal.Causality.inextensible_of_causalCurveOn_eq
declarations.statement: (∀ ⦃d : ℝ → M⦄ ⦃a b : ℝ⦄, C.CausalCurveOn W d a b → ∀ s ∈ Icc a b, ∀ t ∈ Icc a b, d s = d t) → C.CausalCurveIn W I c → C.Inextensible W I c
declarations.standing: Deliverable 1 in the dispatch's words: if every causal curve of W is constant, every causal curve of W is inextensible.

declarations.name: Causal.Causality.not_extensible_of_causalCurveOn_eq
declarations.statement: (∀ ⦃d : ℝ → M⦄ ⦃a b : ℝ⦄, C.CausalCurveOn W d a b → ∀ s ∈ Icc a b, ∀ t ∈ Icc a b, d s = d t) → I.Nonempty → ¬ C.Extensible W I c
declarations.standing: The step. Let (I', c') be a strict extension. c' is constant on I', and c'(φ t) = c t for some t ∈ I, which exists because I is non-empty. So the new point c' t' of StrictlyExtends.grows equals c t. The non-emptiness is needed: over I = ∅ every curve is vacuously extensible, which is why Inextensible carries CausalCurveIn and its `nonempty`.

findings: No paper label is involved: this is a ladder witness. The findings concern the ladder's [[open]] note (programme/ladder.toml, the entry (inextensible_nested, le_nested), ≈ :5767), not ETT.tex.

The note's argument is correct and is now proved model-free, for any causality on any topological space with no instance (Causal.Causality.inextensible_iff_of_causalCurveOn_eq). The precise form: when every causal curve of W over a segment is constant, a curve over I is inextensible iff it is a causal curve over I. The non-emptiness of I, which the note leaves implicit, is what kills StrictlyExtends.grows: over I = ∅ every curve is vacuously extensible.

The note's pointed-line version follows in one line from Causal.Causality.inextensibleNestedOn_of_causalCurveOn_eq with pointedLine_causalCurveOn_eq and spacelikeLine_causalCurveOn_eq. It is not stated: under DEC-167 it would be a no-gluing witness (the dispatch). The name the note wants, Causal.pointedLine_separates_inextensibleNested, is superseded by the rational-line witness.

Stronger than the note: the rational line and the spacelike line are inextensibly nested in each other on every open set, so they have the same inextensible curves (spacelikeLine_inextensibleNestedOn_rationalLine). The spacelike line is also ≤-nested in the rational line (spacelikeLine_leNested_rationalLine). So inextensible nesting both ways, together with ≤-nesting one way, still does not give ≤-nesting the other way.

The converse holds under causal arc-connectedness of the narrower causality on a T1, second countable space (Causal.Causality.InextensibleNestedOn.leNested_of_causallyArcConnected; open-set form le_of_causallyArcConnectedOn). This composes the library's inextensible_nested ⇒ curve_nested with the converse at curve_nested. Every counterexample on the ambient therefore has a narrower causality that is not causally arc-connected, as the rational line is not.
